note: Kniha pečatí testovacích rolí protokolu v5 (balík B7c); nie je to meranie. guest je null: kniha neopisuje hosťa, iba archívy príznakov a finálne behy.

rules.commit_dirty: commit_dirty of the ledger's header and of its created block: whether the working tree differs from the commit (git status --porcelain: a changed, staged or untracked path), the ledger itself and its temporary files aside, since their change is the one the write records (as the records of data/results of tcn/eval.py and scripts/validate_safeguard.py record commit_dirty); null when git is unavailable (verification of B7c, F5)
rules.content: the content fingerprint of a feature archive (content_sha256; the lead's answer to Q31) is the sha256 over the fields of features/archive.py save that are a function of the raw snapshots and their sidecars, and the order of the columns, in this order: mena (the order of the columns, which gives the matrix its meaning), matica (the feature matrix), seq and casy (the sequence number and the time of each row), valid (the validity of each row), perbin and biny (the per-bin values and the identity of the bins, from the sidecars), chain_ids (the chain of each row), snimky (the file name of the snapshot of each row), poznamky (the notes of the traversals of each row), quality_json (the quality of each row) and layout_json (the memory layout of the sidecars); each field adds the line of its name, its numpy dtype (dtype.str, little-endian) and its shape (the integers joined by commas), separated by spaces and ended by a newline, then its bytes in C order; it leaves out trvanie_s (the processing time of each snapshot, which differs at every extraction: the finding of the G0 verification), schema (the version of the archive format, a constant of the code that a replay requires, safeguard/features.py frames_from_archive) and quality_policy and max_medzera_s (parameters of the extraction from the protocol, not of the raw data; the fields they shape, valid and matica, are in); an archive whose arrays cannot be read, or that lacks one of these fields, has no fingerprint (content_sha256 null, and the reason in content_why of its entry in the ledger and of the decision)
rules.guard: a sealed archive of a campaign (one that SEALED_RULE binds to an archive the ledger holds in plan mode campaign) is replayed or scored only inside the final run that consumed its seal (spotrebuj in the process of the final command, python -m tcn.finalne), which lets an archive through when it is an archive of the run or bound to one and every archive of plan mode campaign it is bound to is one of the run's; outside it every guarded entry point refuses it by name before anything is read or written: safeguard replay --archive, tcn.porovnanie replay, safeguard.runtime.replay_archive, the methods of tcn/metody.py and tcn/opisne.py given a window set that holds it, scripts/controls.py outcomes of its controls, the TCN-gui (TCN-gui/analyza.py resolve_input before it opens an input, so analyze, tcn_gui.py with its button Skontrolovať všetky and --png, and TCN-gui/porovnanie.py compare), the legacy activity classifier tcn/klasifikator.py before it loads each archive of an index, the qualification of the feature columns (features/qualification.py from_index, before it opens the archive of a session of a sealed role) and tcn.eval far and udalosti before they read the rows of a replay (by the archive_sha256 its configuration.json names, so by its bytes alone); the raw snapshots of its session likewise (SNAPSHOT_RULE): safeguard replay --snapshots and watch, safeguard.runtime.run_directory (also as the TCN-gui uses it), scripts/validate_safeguard.py and the legacy standalone detector scripts/detektor.py over --snapshots; after the final run it stays refused (the test role is used once)
rules.identity: the identity of a seal is the sha256 of the ASCII lines of the sorted sha256 hex digests of the feature archives (the bytes of the file, features_sha256 of the index) of the sessions of the sealed roles test_benign and test_controls, each line ending in a newline (what sort | sha256sum gives for them); it is no path and no index, so a copy of the corpus under another path has the same seal (skeleton B7 section 7)
rules.rehearsal: an archive of a rehearsal (plan mode rehearsal, proposal 10.4 and 10.5) is kept in the ledger and not enforced: every guard lets through an archive that SEALED_RULE binds to archives of a rehearsal alone (the rehearsal's own, or a re-extraction of one of its sessions) and its decision carries the rehearsal mark, a rehearsal may run the final command more than once (each run recorded with its number), and every output of such a run carries the rehearsal mark (stage generalka on the ledger of record, STAGE_RULE)
rules.run: spotrebuj consumes the seal of a corpus once: in plan mode campaign every sealed archive of the corpus must be in the ledger before (written by the campaign), of that plan, role and session, and none may be in an earlier run; a second final run is refused, also through a copy of the corpus under another path or an index of part of it (the identity is the archives', not the path's), and so is a corpus any of whose sessions, by plan and session id, was in an earlier run of plan mode campaign with another archive (the seal binds the sessions; verification of B7c, F8); the run is recorded in the ledger before any replay, with its archives and its sessions, so a run that fails still consumed the seal (closed with its outcome); one run is open in a process at a time
rules.seal_in_git: at stage final the ledger at HEAD must hold every sealed archive of the corpus before the run begins (seal_in_git true: the commit that holds the seal is the one pushed for its time stamp, TIMESTAMP_RULE); a run whose seal the ledger at HEAD does not hold, or for which that cannot be shown (the ledger outside the repository, git unavailable), is refused before anything is written; at stages generalka and suchy seal_in_git is recorded, not enforced (design B7c 5.2)
rules.sealed: an archive is sealed when the ledger holds it by one of three bindings (the lead's answer to Q31): its bytes (the ledger holds its sha256), its session (the ledger holds an archive of the session id that the directory of an archive given by its path names, read as SNAPSHOT_RULE reads a snapshot directory: the session.json in it, its restore marker, then those of its parent; or the session id its caller names for it, as a window set does for each archive it holds) or its content (the ledger holds an archive of its content fingerprint, CONTENT_RULE); kontrola binds an archive given by its path by all three, and one given by its sha256 by its bytes and by what its caller gives with it, the session id it names (sessions) and the path of the archive (paths), whose directory and content bind it as well: kontrola_okien gives the sessions a window set names for its archives and the paths its index records name (safeguard.training.Windows), tcn.eval the sha256 of a replay alone; a session.json or a restore marker that cannot be read or names no session_id binds no session, and an archive whose arrays cannot be read has no fingerprint: the other bindings decide and the decision says why; zapis writes the archives of the sessions of the sealed roles of a plan with the content fingerprint of each (the campaign at acceptance, package B9; zapis_korpus for a corpus index); an archive bound to none is not sealed: the ledger is the seal, whatever the path or the role a caller names; the seal binds the session and the content, not only the bytes of its archive (verification of B7c, F8; verification of G0, S1): a re-extraction of a sealed session given by its path is sealed by its session in the session's directory and by its content anywhere, and in plan mode campaign zapis refuses a second archive with other bytes for a plan, mode, role and session the ledger holds (a re-extraction is the same session), in plan mode rehearsal it keeps the second one beside the first (REHEARSAL_RULE: not enforced)
rules.snapshots: the raw snapshots of a session enter a detector through kontrola_snimok (verification of B7c, F1): a snapshot directory belongs to the session whose session_id the session.json in it names, or else its restore marker restored_from.json names (a raw/ restored from an archive, RESTORED_RULE, the lead's answer to Q19), or else the session.json and then the restore marker of its parent (the session directory of its raw/); the ledger holds that session when it holds an archive of that session id, and then the archive's rule applies to the directory: refused outside the final run that consumed it (plan mode campaign), the rehearsal mark (plan mode rehearsal); a session.json or a restore marker without a session_id is refused by name, and a directory without a session.json or a restore marker in it or its parent names no session (NO_SESSION_RULE)
rules.stage: the stage of a final run (proposal 11.1) comes from its ledger, never from an option (design B7c 5.1, question Q15): a run on the ledger of record (ZAZNAM, data/results/kniha_pecati.json) has stage final in plan mode campaign and generalka in plan mode rehearsal; a run on any other ledger has stage suchy with the mark of a dry run (a G1 dry run, proposal 10.2, or a test): it proves the logic of the chain, not the science or the sensor, and is never in the text of the thesis (chapter 11.1); the decisions of kontrola carry the stage and the mark of the ledger they consult; vlastna_kniha switches the ledger every guard reads (KNIHA) to a ledger of its own outside data/results for the G1 command, so that its guards refuse its sealed archives as on the ledger of record, and it refuses a path under data/results and an open final run
rules.timestamp: the ledger protects against mistakes, not intent: a person can edit the file; its time stamp is the push of the commit that holds it to the remote repository (proposal 10.6), not its date field; every run records whether the ledger at HEAD held the seals it consumed before it began (seal_in_git: null when the ledger lies outside the repository or git is unavailable), enforced at stage final (SEAL_IN_GIT_RULE)
